parts: Lesson 30: Maintenance of Premises (Module 6A, lesson 30) — Summary

Surfaces are hard (wood, ceramic, metal, marble), semi-hard (linoleum, plastic, paper) or soft (upholstery, jute, linen). Painted walls: dust and remove cobwebs regularly, sponge with warm water and detergent from top to bottom, rinse; never rub vigorously or use coarse abrasives or strong solvents. Wallpaper: gum torn paper back immediately, rub stains with a damp soft cloth, wipe if washable, use grease absorbers (talcum powder, Fuller's earth, bran) for grease stains; never scratch. Ceramic tiles: clean regularly with hot water and detergent; stubborn stains with water sandpaper; do not use too much acid, rinse acids at once. Marble, granite, mosaic and cement: clean with hot water and detergent, wipe corners and sides daily (they get black), occasionally clean with kerosene oil and sawdust, rub with lemon juice to keep marble white and stain-free.

Carpet: clean regularly, once a month take it out, turn it upside down and shake; vacuum; wash colour-fast carpets with soap lather using a brush in circular motions, rinse with a sponge and dry in the sun; naphthalene balls in rolled carpets; air them and dry thoroughly; remove stains at once. Vinyl and linoleum: clean with a squeezed wet cloth, rub stains with mild detergent, scrub corners; do not soak, use hard abrasives or washing soda and alkalis. Coir: clean daily with a coarse broom or brush; shake occasionally; if very dirty wash with soapy water, rinse in cold salty water and dry completely in the open air. Doormats: turn upside down and beat with a stick; wash with soapy water and dry in the sun.
Wooden, metal, glass, cane and plastic surfaces

Plain wood (chopping boards): wash with mild soap and warm water, dry in the open, scrape food with the back of a knife; scrub along the grain, no hard brush, no soaking or very hot water. Polished wood: dust and rub with flannel; remove water marks with methylated spirit, turpentine or mild ammonia. Painted wood: clean with mild soap and water and repaint periodically. Laminate (sunmica): wipe with a wet cloth; remove heat marks with metal polish; use wax polish on veneer. Brass and copper: soap and mild abrasives, lemon juice and salt, vinegar or tamarind pulp with steel wool, sifted ash, old toothbrush for engraved brass, 'Brasso' for ornamental articles (never on cooking utensils: poisonous). Steel: warm soapy water, mild abrasives, soak burnt utensils in salt water. Silver: wash immediately, wrap in tissue paper, remove tea stains with soda and boiling water, 'Silvo'. Iron: clean soon after use, smear oil, remove stains with brick powder, bran or sawdust, dry completely. Non-stick: smear oil before use, rinse at once, sponge and soapy water, no steel wool. Glass: wad of newspaper and water, vinegar in rinse water for shine, ammonia in warm water for grease, methylated spirit for fly specks; no hard scrubbers. Cane: dust and brush corners, wash with warm salty water (1 tablespoon salt per litre), dry in the open, coat with clear varnish. Plastics: kerosene for stubborn stains and put in sun; no strong abrasives or chlorine.

Wear rubber slippers, dry hands, keep a wooden plank or woollen blanket handy and always disconnect the main supply. Fuse: made of thin tin-lead-zinc alloy wire that melts on a short circuit; steps: switch off the main, remove the faulty appliance, take out the fuse cut-out and remove the melted wire, put a new wire through the hole, replace the cut-out and switch on. Sequence: put main switch off, examine and clean the fuse cut-out, replace the wire, put the main switch on. 3-pin plug (5 or 15 amperes): green wire for earthing, red positive, yellow negative; unscrew, expose wires, fix positive and negative parallel without touching, neutral/earth in the lower band, replace the cover. Fans: oil regularly; if it does not start, turn the blades with a stick and switch on: if it picks up speed the capacitor needs changing; noise means worn-out bearings. Room coolers: clean the cabinet, change the grass wool or khus pads every summer, lubricate pump and fan, filter on the water inlet, keep water above the minimum level and switch off before filling. Room heater: replace the heating element; keep the body clean and shiny.

A leaking pipe can only be treated temporarily (cloth or tape); call a plumber. A leaking tap needs a new washer: turn the mains off, unscrew the hand-wheel, remove the headgear (two wrenches, padded one for the lower part), take out the stem and replace the washer. Flushing cistern: pulling the lever raises the bell-shaped unit; water flows, creating vacuum; the float (ball valve) falls, opening the inlet valve; it rises to close the inlet at a set level. Faults: worn washer in the inlet valve (repair like a tap); jammed valve (open and clean); impurities in the tank (clean periodically); ball corroded or punctured so it does not rise and water overflows (change the ball).
